1370.skill_description: Conduct follow-up calls or face-to-face interviews as planned after counseling, remind the client to notice and record new experiences, feelings, or thoughts, understand mood, functioning, and life adaptation, adjust recommendations or refer again if necessary, to prevent overlooking residual issues and continuously monitor changes.
1370.when_to_use: At the end of each session and during the self-monitoring stage at home, or at phase points in the follow-up stage after termination.
1370.trigger: Client's recent status is unclear, environmental changes are occurring; there are still concerns or new experiences and thoughts that need follow-up; previous follow-up indicated items to be followed up.

1319.skill_name: Re-measure SAS/SDS to Compare Residuals and Trends
1319.skill_description: Re-administer scales such as SAS, SDS (combined with SCL-90 when necessary) during the termination or follow-up phase, compare with previous or initial assessment data, quantify anxiety and depression levels and factor changes, judge whether there are residuals and the extent of improvement, to provide a basis for termination decisions, subsequent consolidation, and self-monitoring.
1319.when_to_use: During the termination and consolidation phase or phase-specific follow-ups, when objective assessment of efficacy and the presence of residual anxiety/depression is required.
1319.trigger: Client reports subjective improvement but still experiences discomfort such as tension, insomnia, unstable attention; entering the review and re-measurement phase or when deciding whether to terminate the counseling relationship.

1290.skill_name: Interview and Multi-source Feedback Assessment of Functional Residuals
1290.skill_description: Combine interview observations and client self-report, focus on indicators such as emotional stability, verbal expression, interpersonal relationships, and learning/life, and solicit feedback from teachers/classmates and review assignments, quantify the current situation, and comprehensively judge whether symptoms or social functioning limitations still exist and the trend of change.
1290.when_to_use: During the consolidation and termination phase or for effect assessment and follow-up review, when judging functional recovery and the scope of residual impact is necessary.
1290.trigger: Emotional/expression clues appear during the interview; feedback from others indicates problems; client quantifies the current situation or shares experiences with assignments and interactions still show fluctuations.

1300.skill_name: Arrange short-term follow-up to track quantitative status
1300.skill_description: Arrange follow-up at designated points one month after completion. In the interview, invite visitors to share learning, interpersonal, and emotional changes, and conduct scoring and comparison to verify if residual symptoms have subsided and function has recovered, providing a basis for subsequent self-management and follow-up.
1300.when_to_use: During short-term follow-up after consultation or follow-up visits three to nine months later, used to assess consolidation effects and residual issues.
1300.trigger: Need to confirm improvement and maintenance of school life after a certain period; when self-rating scores fluctuate or reports are occasionally affected by stress, tracking is needed.

1407.skill_name: Regular follow-up to monitor residual symptoms and function
1407.skill_description: Conduct phone calls or face-to-face interviews as scheduled during follow-up after completion. Systematically check recent mood, sleep, appetite, and social functioning, record frequency and intensity, verify goal achievement, identify remaining symptoms and functional limitations, and adjust recommendations or continue observation if necessary.
1407.when_to_use: Follow-up nodes during the completion and consolidation phase (e.g., one month later or at the start of a new school term), used to understand the subsequent status and residual issues.
1407.trigger: Client initiates follow-up or reaches the agreed time; complaints of insomnia, mild anxiety/depression, or functional limitations; when dynamic status needs to be grasped.

1287.skill_name: Follow-up combined with scales to quantitatively monitor residual and trends
1287.skill_description: At the completion and follow-up nodes, combine scales such as SDS, SAS, BDI, and subjective distress checks from 0-10, assessing four aspects: physical, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning. Compare life feedback with changes in scores for the same scale factor. Assist with re-examination if necessary to form trackable indicators, continuously observe residual status and trends.
1287.when_to_use: When objectively understanding the degree of residual status and change trends is needed at the completion stage and subsequent follow-ups, or when subjective improvement needs to be verified after the start of a new school term.
1287.trigger: Symptoms still present at the end or scales are in the positive critical range; when comprehensive assessment is needed based on client's self-report of distress or changes in scale scores.

1474.skill_name: Continuous relaxation training and monitoring improvement
1474.skill_description: Assign daily 20–30 minutes of breathing/muscle relaxation exercises and require recording completion and changes in mood before and after the exercise. Clarify autonomous application before sleep and during anxiety. Check and reinforce execution during follow-up, as a self-treatment and process indicator, to alleviate tension and difficulty falling asleep, tracking improvement in sleep, mood, and function until stable.
1474.when_to_use: During the later consultation phase and home consolidation phase, or when residual tension, anxiety, and sleep difficulties exist, continuous self-intervention and monitoring are needed.
1474.trigger: Occurrence of difficulty falling asleep, anxiety/palpitations, muscle tension, increased heart rate, emotional excitement, or incomplete exercise records, or decreased persistence.

1455.skill_name: Re-test SCL-90 and compare residual and change
1455.skill_description: Refer to SCL-90 scores, positive items, and factor changes at the initial assessment and at the end or follow-up, combine with SAS/SDS if necessary, compare pre- and post-data, quantify improvement in somaticization, anxiety, interpersonal dimensions, and areas that remain high, to judge if there is any residual or trend, to provide basis for self-monitoring and subsequent arrangements.
1455.when_to_use: During consultation termination or follow-up, when needing to objectify symptom changes and define residual issues.
1455.trigger: When quantifying changes in anxiety or other symptoms; when the client reports improvement but still feels discomfort, or when scale scores do not significantly decrease/approach the upper limit of the norm, needs to be checked.

1373.skill_name: Review and affirm specific changes and methods
1373.skill_description: Review and name the gains in the consultation, such as progress in emotion management, rational thinking, diaphragmatic breathing and meditation, cognitive shifts, behavioral activation, recovery of sleep and interest, point out specific examples and stage achievements, provide positive feedback, reinforce self-efficacy and motivation to continue using them.
1373.when_to_use: During the review and consolidation phase of gains, such as at the fifth, sixth session, or during follow-up, needs to summarize and consolidate achievements.
1373.trigger: When the client can describe their changes or mastered methods and has experienced positive effects; when scales/records show improvement (e.g., decrease in frequency and duration, sleep improvement, increased activity).

1458.skill_name: Encourage transferring learned skills to life and relationships
1458.skill_description: Based on summarizing effective practices, encourage continuing to travel, socialize, go shopping, reconnect with classmates and roommates, and practice positive communication, extend cognitive and relaxation skills to broader contexts; at the same time, extract the role and applicable situations of self-help strategies such as emotional release, positive self-suggestion, communication with others, and exercise, to promote continued use and deepening.
1458.when_to_use: During the extension of gains before termination and planning subsequent plans, or during the follow-up period when promoting effective practices to new scenarios.
1458.trigger: When the client's functioning has improved and is willing to expand the scope of application; when they can recall and share regulating methods used and their effects, seeking continued use in other scenarios.

1272.skill_name: Encourage experience transfer and sustained application
1272.skill_description: Make the effective experiences refined in review specific to learning, homework, class participation, interpersonal communication, and interest cultivation scenarios, encourage using psychological knowledge and skills to adjust perceptions and emotions, improve interactions with others, form continuous action to enhance ease and confidence and extend to daily life.
1272.when_to_use: During the consolidation and termination phase, after summarizing, needs to transform experiences into continuous action and generalization.
1272.trigger: When the client expresses willingness to improve learning, interpersonal, and lifestyle habits, and discusses how to extend consultation gains or seek scenario-based application suggestions.

1284.skill_name: Guide review and affirm consultation benefits
1284.skill_description: Prompt the client to summarize benefits with specific examples, such as emotional relief, increased learning motivation and goal clarity, improved memory and thinking, richer interpersonal relationships, sleep restoration, self-acceptance, and enhanced self-confidence; review learning and change mechanisms, provide affirmation and positive attention, consolidate self-efficacy, and maintain motivation.
1284.when_to_use: In the consolidation and summary phase or at the end of the session, used to review the consultation process and outcomes, consolidate benefits and self-efficacy.
1284.trigger: The client can review and state changes, present examples of improvement, or self-report improvement, but may still show self-doubt or insufficient motivation.

1424.skill_name: Summarize and consolidate cognitive change methods
1424.skill_description: Guide the client to review and verbalize the steps of "identify unreasonable beliefs—debate—replace with rational beliefs," clarify which approaches are most effective and the reasons, emphasize continuous practice to solidify new concepts and maintain emotional improvement.
1424.when_to_use: In the re-education and summary phase, needed to consolidate consultation effects and review sustainable tools.
1424.trigger: The client indicates they have learned emotional regulation or can give examples of cognitive shifts leading to improvement.

1451.skill_name: Promote skill transfer and broad application
1451.skill_description: Guide the client to apply emotion regulation and cognitive adjustment strategies to learning and daily life situations, discuss feasible scenarios and specific steps, and rehearse usage in key moments; identify and affirm positive life changes (such as improved sleep, increased confidence, social expansion), connect positive feedback, encourage continuous use and expansion in social groups and family.
1451.when_to_use: When planning for post-consultation self-practice and skill broadening, or in the phase of reviewing benefits and strengthening motivation.
1451.trigger: The client wishes to use the methods in new scenarios, or has mentioned specific progress and is willing to expand application.

1429.skill_name: Review and consolidate methods and encourage practice
1429.skill_description: Review key techniques mastered in consultation (such as rational emotion debate, gradual relaxation, exposure and anxiety rating scales, acceptance techniques, etc.), invite the client to restate consultation points and coping strategies, restate operational points, reinforce rational concepts and positive self-awareness, encourage continuous daily practice and application.
1429.when_to_use: In the review and summary phase at the end, needed to fix what has been learned and promote daily application.
1429.trigger: The client has learned and is practicing related methods at home, or has achieved improvement and asked how to continue applying them.

1434.skill_description: Remind the client to continue practicing learned methods in future life, review consultation notes for self-encouragement and adjustment during emotional fluctuations; continuously apply and optimize strategies when facing new difficulties to maintain existing achievements and further improve interpersonal and emotional adaptation.
1434.when_to_use: During the consolidation of session summaries and action plans, and during subsequent self-maintenance and follow-up intervals.
1434.trigger: When the client acknowledges current gains but may still face challenges, or when experiencing emotional fluctuations, decreased motivation, or needing to review learned content.

1398.skill_name: Inventory and Name Acquired Skills and Resources
1398.skill_description: Summarize and name transferable abilities such as emotional regulation, cognitive reframing of absolutistic cognitions, objective self-awareness, active expression, and seeking social support, clarify the value and applicable scenarios of these 'tools', and create a list of skills to take away for later self-use.
1398.when_to_use: During the gains inventory phase before ending a consultation, when systematically reviewing personal growth and skill acquisition.
1398.trigger: Self-assessment/other assessment shows the ability to better control emotions, express needs, plan learning, or participate in activities.

1435.skill_name: Link Growth Gains with Future Goals
1435.skill_description: Help the client name the gains in emotional management, social skills, and cognitive restructuring, review successful experiences, and connect them with future planning, interests, and important life scenarios, clarifying the direction and goals for subsequent application.
1435.when_to_use: During the gains inventory and outlook phase before ending, to promote skill generalization and goal alignment.
1435.trigger: When the client mentions having plans for the future, seeking interests, or reporting increased sense of meaning.

1425.skill_name: Strengthen Resilience to Setbacks and Help-Seeking Awareness
1425.skill_description: Discuss the universality of setbacks and positive coping, encourage the use of rational beliefs when encountering difficulties and actively seeking help, enhancing the ability to withstand and adapt to challenges, preventing catastrophic thinking.
1425.when_to_use: During the summary phase, for clients who are still worried about the future or prone to catastrophic thinking.
1425.trigger: When the client talks about worry about repeated failure, unease about the future, or experiencing catastrophic thinking.

1452.skill_description: Highlight positive changes in review, such as decreased anxiety scores, improved learning efficiency, and improved relationships, provide specific positive feedback to help internalize a sense of accomplishment, enhance self-efficacy and maintain motivation, and support the continued use of learned material.
1452.when_to_use: Key periods for consolidating gains, enhancing persistence motivation, and confidence.
1452.trigger: Significant progress shown in assessment/self-report, or when the client doubts the effectiveness or motivation decreases.

1310.skill_name: Collaboratively Develop Subsequent Practice Checklist and Goals
1310.skill_description: Develop personalized subsequent practice checklists and goals with the client (e.g., exams, skill practice, continuous recording of negative events), clarify execution steps, frequency, and support channels, acknowledge their feasible plan, and encourage adherence, promoting the continuation and life-application of skills.
1310.when_to_use: In the concluding phase or consolidation sessions, planning subsequent practice to deepen gains.
1310.trigger: Client proposes future learning or practice goals and is willing to implement the plan, or seeks acknowledgment and support for specific plans.

1308.skill_name: Inventory and Name Cognitive and Self-Help Skills
1308.skill_description: Guide the review and naming of mastered cognitive and self-help skills, such as identifying dysfunctional thoughts, distinguishing subjective and objective, relaxation training, positive self-talk, and rational evaluation/refutation, clarifying applicable situations and operational points, forming a personal tool list.
1308.when_to_use: During the review of gains in the concluding or consolidation session, when systematically reviewing skills is needed.
1308.trigger: Client can recall and report specific skills practiced in daily life, such as relaxation and identifying automatic thoughts, and their effects.

1265.skill_name: Arrange and Sustain Thought Record Practice
1265.skill_description: Clarify the frequency of thought record practice, trigger scenarios, and recording points, encourage its use in learning and life; combine with a self-affirmation list to enhance awareness of strengths, serving as a long-term self-help tool to stabilize and generalize cognitive changes.
1265.when_to_use: During the skill transfer and consolidation phase, or when entering the self-help and follow-up interval period after completion.
1265.trigger: Occurrence of automatic thoughts and emotional fluctuations, or self-deprecation and low confidence, requiring a sustainable self-help tool.

1309.skill_name: Encourage broad application and continuous practice in multiple contexts
1309.skill_description: Encourage continuous practice of what has been learned in contexts such as social, interpersonal, and academic settings, such as proactive socializing, family communication, and academic goal execution, and track the application effects to expand and stabilize consulting gains.
1309.when_to_use: When concluding and follow-up arrangements, the consulting outcomes need to be transferred to broader life domains.
1309.trigger: Client shares application cases or expresses the desire and concerns to expand application in social, learning, or family settings.

1441.skill_name: Strengthen self-efficacy and sense of control
1441.skill_description: Help identify evidence of increased sense of control and competence (ability to think calmly and express accurately, confidently share coping methods), name growth and provide concrete affirmation, enhancing confidence for continued practice and transfer application.
1441.when_to_use: When summarizing the dimensions of growth in consulting gains, consolidating self-efficacy, and enhancing motivation for practice.
1441.trigger: Client expresses more confidence in handling emotions or shares successful coping experiences and methods.

1381.skill_name: Inventory and consolidate cognitive and behavioral strategy lists
1381.skill_description: Systematically organize the tools learned in consulting, such as cognitive restructuring, attention training, and safety behavior relinquishment, list learned methods and application scenarios, confirm actionable steps, form a sustainable strategy list, and encourage daily practice.
1381.when_to_use: When inventorying consulting gains and evaluating outcomes, a sustainable strategy list needs to be formed.
1381.trigger: Client reports being able to use learned strategies and experiencing improvement in emotions and functioning.

1267.skill_name: Write and review consulting notes and transfer application
1267.skill_description: After the session, review with the client the insights and solutions that can be recorded, forming consulting notes; look up and apply, examine effects, and adjust strategies in similar contexts, consolidating gains and promoting cross-context transfer.
1267.when_to_use: During the summary and consolidation phase after each session or before concluding, inventorying gains and practicing transfer is needed.
1267.trigger: Client gains new insights or faces repetitive problems, needing to use existing records and plans.

1289.skill_name: Identify and strengthen personal strengths and self-appraisal
1289.skill_description: Collaboratively sort out the client's strengths and provide evidence, use self-other feedback to affirm their strengths and self-analytical behaviors, consolidate positive self-appraisal and confidence, support long-term growth and self-efficacy enhancement.
1289.when_to_use: When reviewing gains in the sixth session and subsequent sessions, used to strengthen self-appraisal and confidence.
1289.trigger: Completion of 'find strengths' type homework or the ability to list and substantiate personal strengths, or receiving positive feedback from others.

1344.skill_name: Create and use a self-affirmation list
1344.skill_description: Guide the client to list personal strengths and achievements, use with thought records to reinforce attention to and affirmation of positive aspects of oneself, enhance self-esteem and confidence, support self-encouragement and cognitive correction in daily situations.
1344.when_to_use: When the stage requires strengthening the sense of self-worth, or when self-deprecation still occurs intermittently.
1344.trigger: Client reports fluctuations in self-esteem, guilt or self-blame, or difficulty seeing one's strengths in a review.

1292.skill_name: Strengthen new practices in interpersonal and self-management
1292.skill_description: Invite the client to share new practice experiences such as communicating with parents or interacting with roommates, review key practices and provide affirmation and reinforcement, promote transfer and maintenance in interpersonal and self-management.
1292.when_to_use: During homework feedback and gain review stages, used to consolidate changes in real-life situations.
1292.trigger: Client reports specific new attempts and positive experiences in communication, interpersonal relationships, or self-management.

1299.skill_name: Follow-up to confirm maintenance and expansion of gains
1299.skill_description: In the follow-up, jointly review progress in peer relationships and academics, confirm that the consulting gains are maintained and expanded in reality, and clarify specific practices and application scenarios to continue.
1299.when_to_use: Follow-up one month later or subsequent follow-ups, summarizing the extension and consolidation of gains in multiple contexts.
1299.trigger: Client reports sustained improvement in school performance, interpersonal relationships, and grades, requiring consolidation and extension of practices.

1340.skill_name: Transferring Communication and Relationship Strategies to Multiple Scenarios
1340.skill_description: Reviewing the sense of relationship repair and support gained from actively befriending like-minded friends, proactively communicating and sharing with parents, and distilling key points to develop specific exercises and self-monitoring in new contexts such as campus, family, and clubs, encouraging the continuous building of supportive relational networks to solidify social confidence.
1340.when_to_use: When reviewing relationship improvement and planning for continuous promotion in contexts such as campus and family.
1340.trigger: When positive signs such as making new friends, reconciling with parents, increased communication, or reduced conflict appear, and the willingness to apply what has been learned in more scenarios.

1430.skill_name: Inventorying Transferable Tool List and Corresponding Scenarios
1430.skill_description: Jointly listing transferable tools with the client (such as the five-column chart/ABC rational thinking and debate, support-rebuttal, behavioral experiments, relaxation and meditation, interpersonal skills, coping cards) and corresponding them to specific scenarios in their daily emotional management and interpersonal interactions, clarifying reusable tools.
1430.when_to_use: During the inventorying phase of gains, when transforming implicit experience into actionable tools and confirming mastery.
1430.trigger: When the client can recall and describe specific techniques used and their effects, or brings homework records/verbal reports of their use in daily life.

1445.skill_name: Identifying and Mobilizing Social Support Systems
1445.skill_description: Inventorying and naming support resources such as friends, family, roommates, psychological center, advisor, and doctor, along with their help, clarifying contact methods and timing for use, and planning to proactively connect and expand when needed, to serve as stable external resources for maintaining and expanding gains.
1445.when_to_use: During the gains summary and resource planning phase, when arranging subsequent support connections and follow-up paths.
1445.trigger: When the client experiences emotional improvement and increased confidence from the support of relatives and friends, or has connected to campus resources and is willing to use them continuously.

1422.skill_name: Arranging Interpersonal Skills Training and Promoting Application
1422.skill_description: Arranging participation in interpersonal and communication group counseling or teaching specific communication skills; reviewing key points after the course/exercise and selecting real-life scenarios such as dorms or classes for continuous practice and application, consolidating interpersonal skills and promoting generalization.
1422.when_to_use: When needing to improve interpersonal communication skills and transfer consultation gains to daily situations.
1422.trigger: When the client shows a lack of or has gained initial confidence in interpersonal interactions, requiring practical training and subsequent application consolidation.

1296.skill_name: Promote and apply rational beliefs in multiple contexts
1296.skill_description: Synthesize established rational beliefs and life guidance (such as letting things be, lowering expectations, participating in activities, and active communication), encourage continuous application in family, interpersonal, and academic contexts, positively reinforce new cognitive and behavioral patterns, and develop implementation plans to prevent relapse.
1296.when_to_use: After effect assessment or before ending the session, to summarize growth gains and plan for daily practice.
1296.trigger: The client has formed and demonstrated new rational beliefs and behavioral patterns, with positive changes in attitude and engagement.

1298.skill_name: Summarize and review the list of rational beliefs
1298.skill_description: Organize the rational core beliefs extracted during counseling into a list, arrange for daily short reviews and self-dialogue practice, consolidate the replacement and internalization of irrational beliefs, and stabilize the new cognitive system.
1298.when_to_use: When the client is ready for consolidation exercises and follow-up during the post-cognitive restructuring phase.
1298.trigger: Rational belief statements have been identified and formed, and the client has the willingness and conditions to engage in daily self-practice.

1278.skill_name: Consolidate cognitive restructuring and new concepts
1278.skill_description: Review the changes brought about by cognitive restructuring, compare each item with old concepts and new adaptive beliefs, identify and challenge irrational beliefs such as "not being loved/life is rotten," clarify the mechanism of change and evidence, use cognitive review to reinforce rational beliefs and healthy coping patterns.
1278.when_to_use: During consolidation sessions to review counseling outcomes, clarify the mechanism of change, and transferable experiences.
1278.trigger: The client can provide examples of conceptual shifts and identify limitations of old cognitions, or intermittent old negative automatic thoughts still appear and need to be summarized.

1276.skill_name: Review and summarize the effective application of CBT techniques
1276.skill_description: Review the application of evidence, feasibility analysis, exception experiences, and behavioral experiments in alleviating anxiety and changing cognitions, clarify which techniques are most effective for them and applicable contexts, as replicable experiences.
1276.when_to_use: In preparation for the ending or consolidation phase, when methods' benefits and replicable experiences need to be refined.
1276.trigger: The client can give examples of using CBT techniques in life and achieving positive results.

1318.skill_name: Develop CBT Skill Transfer and Application Plan
1318.skill_description: Collaborate with the client to clarify specific ways to use CBT tools such as identifying emotions and adjusting thoughts in life, learning, and work settings, set realistic expectations and goals, and form an actionable plan for daily use and coping.
1318.when_to_use: In the termination phase or early follow-up, when planning specific plans for future use and relapse prevention.
1318.trigger: When the client asks how to apply it in daily life, or when about to enter a new situation (work, study) and expresses goals and concerns.

1339.skill_description: Clarify continuing mindfulness practice (such as breathing, walking), cultivate observational self, and use cognitive defusion; review its benefits for attention and emotion regulation, sleep, and sense of hope; develop daily practice frequency and settings to maintain stability and prevent relapse.
1339.when_to_use: In the benefit review and consolidation phase, when developing daily maintenance and relapse prevention plans.
1339.trigger: When the client benefits from the practice and wishes to continue, or when signals requiring emotional regulation consolidation such as tension, anxiety, or sleep disturbance appear.

1355.skill_name: Review and Promote Self-Help Skills like Breathing Relaxation
1355.skill_description: Review and (if necessary) teach simple breathing relaxation training, clarify the key points for its use during high stress, insomnia, inattention, and restlessness, encourage continued daily practice and application in daily situations such as the dormitory or classroom, to consolidate effects and prevent recurrence.
1355.when_to_use: After effect assessment or in the termination and consolidation phase, when sorting available tools and developing a daily use plan.
1355.trigger: When the client mentions using relaxation techniques to alleviate distress, reports anxiety/palpitations, or wishes to apply relaxation training in other settings.
